use: The opening cover of a deck: a large presentation title with a subtitle beneath it.
A bold cover: an oversized presentation title at top-left with the subtitle set in the bottom-right corner.
An agenda / index: a heading on the left and a numbered list of up to nine sections on the right.
An index that lists a few major sections with their page-ranges, anchored to the bottom of the slide.
An index laid out as a two-column grid of numbered sections, each with a title and a one-line description.
An index as a two-column grid of numbered section titles, each row divided by a hairline.
A chapter / section divider: a large section number and title marking a new part of the deck.
A large statement title with a section number below it, centred on the slide.
A confidentiality / legal statement anchored to the bottom of the slide.
A confidentiality / legal statement centred on the slide.
A confidentiality / legal statement with the heading at the top and the paragraph at the bottom.
A text-heavy overview: a heading and subtitle above a couple of body paragraphs in the left column.
An executive summary: a heading on the left with the summary text set in two columns on the right.
An executive summary with the heading on top and the summary text flowing across three columns.
An executive summary with the heading on top and the summary text as full-width paragraphs below.
An executive summary with the heading centred in the upper area and the summary anchored to the bottom.
A cover letter / note to the client: a heading on the left with the message set in two columns on the right.
A cover letter / note to the client: a heading on the left with a single wide column of text, vertically centred.
A cover letter / note to the client: a heading with the full message set as a single block below it.
A cover letter / note to the client: a heading at the top with the message centred in the space below.
A cover letter / note to the client alongside a full-height team photo on the right.
A full-page statement or pull-quote, left-aligned, with an attribution.
A statement or pull-quote indented from the left margin, with an attribution.
A statement or pull-quote on a mint-green background, indented from the left.
A centred statement quote in two sizes — a smaller lead line above a larger emphasised line — with an attribution.
A statement quote alongside a square photo on the right.
A statement quote alongside a full-height photo on the right.
A positioning statement with an intro on the left and a two-column grid of headline figures on the right.
A bold heading on the left with supporting grey body paragraphs on the right.
A heading with two grey text columns across the top and a full-width photo below.
A full-width heading over three value cards, each with a mint icon, a title and body.
A short section label on the left paired with a large grey impact statement on the right.
A bold heading with a grey supporting caption on the left, alongside a full-height photo on the right.
A grey lead heading and a bold closing heading on the left, with a three-photo mosaic on the right.
A full-bleed team photo with a teal veil and a cluster of translucent headline-figure bubbles.
The seven Nagarro caring values as mint line icons under a scripted 'Our caring values' heading, on petrol black.
A dense icon grid of service offerings / capabilities — the 'what we do' wall.
A three-phase process comparison with bullet benefits, tool chips, and stat callouts.
A single-phase deep dive: challenges vs. AI acceleration, tool rows, impact stats, and a Transformation callout.
A large question/heading on the left with two columns of bold-led explanatory paragraphs.
A full-width heading over three columns of bold-led explanatory paragraphs.
A 'trusted by' client logo wall — heading left, 3×4 logo grid right.
A dense 'trusted by' client logo wall — heading left, 3×7 logo grid right.
A headingless full-width client logo wall — a 4×5 grid of logos.
An industry-segmented client logo wall — categories in two columns, each a labelled row of logos.
A dark regional client logo wall — eyebrow + heading left, 4×5 logo grid right on petrol-black.
A dark capability overview — a client logo wall beside two 'bubble chain' panels (areas, technology).
A full-bleed photo statement — one large white sentence over a full-page image.
A full-bleed photo statement with a longer, two-line white sentence.
A full-bleed photo statement — a wide image (e.g. a paired landmark shot) with one white sentence overlaid.
A full-bleed photo statement — one large white sentence over a full-page image.
A results/proof-point statement over a full-bleed product-collage image (device mockup + screenshots).
A co-brand partnership slide — a partner wordmark + nagarro lockup on a dark gradient, with a tagline.
The opening cover of a deck: presentation title and subtitle, with company / date / project details.
Table of contents / agenda: a heading and intro on the left, a numbered list of up to nine sections with page numbers on the right.
A bold table of contents / agenda: up to five sections as large numbered rows.
A chapter / section divider: a large section number and title marking a new part of the deck.
A detailed table of contents: a heading on the left and a 2×3 grid of up to six numbered sections, each with sub-items.
A photo mosaic of five images — a 2×2 grid on the left plus one tall image on the right — under a section header. Visual, image-led.
A text-only content slide: a section heading on the left and an intro paragraph on the right.
A header with title and body, plus one full-width image below. Text-led with a supporting visual.
A header with intro, then two large photos side by side. Text-led with two supporting visuals.
A header with intro, then three photos side by side. Text-led with three supporting visuals.
A header with intro, then a photo mosaic — a narrow column of two stacked images beside two larger images.
Mirror of content-grid-6-photo — two large images beside a narrow stacked column, header with intro above.
A dense photo wall: eight images in a 4×2 grid filling the slide. Purely visual.
Eight photo cards in a 4×2 grid, each with a title and short caption. A dense catalogue or highlights wall.
A mirrored split: two stacked photos on the left, a heading and paragraph on the right.
A split layout: a heading and paragraph on the left, a 2×2 grid of photos on the right.
Three image cards in a row — each with a photo, title, subtitle and short body. Services, values or highlights.
Three portrait photos with a name and role beneath each. A team or leadership row.
A split layout: a heading and paragraph on the left, three photos on the right.
One large photo beside a text column with a heading and paragraph. Balanced image + copy.
Mirror of content-twocol-photo — a text column on the left and one large photo on the right.
A header, then up to three rows each pairing a short title with an explanatory paragraph.
A heading and paragraph on the left beside one large photo on the right. A single featured card.
Four photo cards in a row — each with a photo, title, subtitle and short body.
Five photo cards in a row — each with a photo, title, subtitle and short body.
A header with intro, then a 2×3 grid of six photos.
A header with intro, then a 4×2 grid of eight photos.
A header with intro, then a 4×2 grid of eight photo cards, each with a title and short caption.
A header with intro, then a 3×3 grid of nine photos.
A header, then a grid of photos each with a short caption and a number badge overlaid — a ranked or numbered set.
A staggered three-column layout mixing three photos with two text cards. Editorial, magazine-like.
A two-column layout: one large photo beside a text card and a second photo. Editorial split.
Mirror of cards-split-3-photo — a staggered three-column layout mixing three photos with two text cards.
Mirror of cards-split-2-photo — a text card and photo beside one large photo.
An intro panel with category pills on the left beside a 2×3 grid of six tinted text cards. No imagery.
Mirror of cards-split-6 — a 2×3 grid of six tinted text cards beside an intro panel on the right.
A header, then a 2×3 grid of six text cards — each a title with a short paragraph. No imagery.
A header, then four text cards in a row — each a title with a short paragraph. No imagery.
A header, then five text cards in a row — each a title with a short paragraph. No imagery.
A photo wall: six images in a 2×3 grid filling the slide.
A photo wall: eight images in a 4×2 grid filling the slide.
A dense photo wall: eighteen images in a 6×3 grid. A contact sheet or large gallery.
One large photo filling the slide body between the top bar and footer.
A single photo bleeding edge to edge, no logo or footer. Maximum visual impact.
A photo mosaic: one large image on the left, a wide image and a pair of images on the right.
A photo mosaic: one wide image beside two tall images.
A photo wall: six images in a 3×2 grid filling the slide.
A photo wall variant: six images in a 2×3 grid of taller tiles.
A heading and paragraph on the left beside one large photo on the right.
Mirror of gallery-split-photo — one large photo on the left, a heading and paragraph on the right.
A staggered three-column layout mixing three photos and two text blocks under a heading. Editorial gallery.
Mirror of gallery-split-3-photo — a staggered three-column layout of three photos and two text blocks.
A heading and paragraph on the left beside a photo stack — one wide image over a pair.
Mirror of gallery-split-2-photo — a photo stack on the left, a heading and paragraph on the right.
A text column (heading, paragraphs, category pills) beside one large photo with a caption underneath.
Four portrait photos with a name and role beneath each. A team or leadership row.
Five portrait photos with a name and role beneath each. A team or leadership row.
A heading with context and category pills on the left beside a large quotation on the right.
A full-page quotation or statement, set large in quotation marks.
A full-page quotation set large (Heading1 scale), attributed to a person — name, title and company.
A supporting photo on the left beside a large quotation on the right.
Mirror of quote-split-photo — a large quotation on the left beside a supporting photo on the right.
A header, then up to three rows each with a title and two text columns — a simple comparison or spec table.
The closing slide: a large thank-you headline and contact details (email, website).
Portfolio opening cover: a top info row (role / specialised in / contact / about) with a large display title pinned bottom-left.
Portfolio cover variant: cover info + display title on the left, a full-height photo on the right.
A big centered statement with an inline photo chip embedded in the sentence.
Portfolio index / table of contents: sections with right-aligned page numbers.
Portfolio table of contents with right-aligned page ranges.
CV/about page: a full-height photo on the left, an About paragraph and an Experience list on the right.
CV/about page: a photo + About paragraph on the left, an Experience list on the right.
A page header (title + intro) above two large side-by-side photos.
A bio column (heading + short entries + traits) beside a full-height photo.
A grid of labelled service tiles beside a heading + paragraph.
A skills eyebrow + numbered skills list at the bottom-left, beside a full-height photo.
A skills eyebrow + two plain columns of skills, vertically centered.
A section divider: one oversized muted word, vertically centered.
A visual table of contents: a numbered project list beside a grid of project thumbnails.
Four project columns, each a heading, a list of services, and a photo below.
Five project columns, each a heading, a list of services, and a photo below.
A project divider: one oversized muted word, vertically centered.
A project brief: a heading + paragraph at the top, a Year / Category / Link meta row at the bottom.
A heading top-left + paragraph bottom-left, beside a full-height photo.
A heading + paragraph on the left, a two-column photo collage on the right.
A project detail: title + client + meta on the left, two columns of body copy on the right.
A project intro: title / client / year + two columns of body copy above a full-width photo.
A small project header above a large full-width photo.
A full-frame 2×2 collage of project photos.
A full-height photo on the left, a Results heading + headline stats on the right.
A heading on the left, a large testimonial quote with attribution on the right.
A project divider: one oversized muted word, vertically centered.
Two stacked sections, each a heading on the left and a body paragraph on the right.
A heading + paragraph on a narrow left column, a 3-column grid of photos on the right.
A project header (title / client / year + body columns) above a row of photos.
A grid of photos on top, a project header (title / client + body columns) below.
A narrow project detail on the left, a collage of photos filling the right.
A full-bleed photo wall — a brick-offset grid of images running off every edge, no chrome.
A full-bleed pairing: one large photo on the left, a 2×2 grid of photos on the right.
A full-bleed photo collage of six photos in two columns.
A project divider: one oversized muted word, vertically centered.
A project brief: a heading + paragraph at the top, a Year / Category / Link meta row at the bottom.
A project case study: header + intro on top, then a photo beside Approach / Outcomes write-ups.
A project header (title / client / year + body columns) above a row of photos.
A project name / client + body on a narrow left column, a 3-column grid of photos on the right.
A project header, a row of tall story-format photos, and a meta row.
A full-bleed pairing: one large photo on the left, a wide photo over two photos on the right.
A heading + paragraph on a narrow left column, a centered 3×3 grid of square thumbnails on the right.
A header (title + intro) above a 4-column grid of photos.
A heading on the left, a stack of short testimonial quotes with attribution on the right.
A heading + supporting photo on the left, a large testimonial quote on the right.
A heading above a list of awards / recognitions with years.
A heading above two columns of award names with count numbers in brand accent colours.
A heading + a list of press mentions on the left, a full-height photo on the right.
A heading above a table of projects (Project / Client / Service / Comments / Link).
A closing contact slide: big heading + a photo, phone / web, and a table of social handles.
The closing: an oversized muted sign-off, vertically centered.
The opening cover of a financial report: a bold report title + muted subtitle, with a company / date sign-off.
A legal / disclaimer page: a big muted heading plus dense labelled fine-print (safe-harbor, non-GAAP, trademarks) in a panel.
A header, then a short stack of headline statements (each a bold metric sentence), with a supporting image alongside.
A highlights wall: press quotes and headline stats as dark / grey cards in a three-column masonry — an at-a-glance proof grid.
A headline growth metric in words, proven by a filled area / line chart of the trend over time.
A headline metric in words with a supporting paragraph, plus a stacked proportion bar showing a split (e.g. revenue by channel).
A headline metric stated in words, proven by a vertical bar chart of the trend across periods.
A headline count in words, illustrated by two dot-waffle cards where each dot represents one unit (deals, customers, wins).
A stacked bar chart breaking each period's total into segments (e.g. revenue by geography), with the total called out above each bar.
A grouped financial table where each group of metric rows is followed by a dark Total summary band.
A stacked bar chart of percentage composition per period (e.g. expense ratios), panelled with a legend.
A dotted-line trend chart in a panel — a soft way to show a fairly flat metric (e.g. gross margin) holding steady over time.
A narrative on the left with a multi-line trend chart on the right — e.g. actual revenue vs. projection over several years.
A narrative on the left with a pie chart on the right — a revenue / share breakdown across a handful of partners or segments.
A narrative on the left with a radar chart on the right — comparing performance across several products or dimensions at a glance.
A narrative + legend on the left with a two-segment stacked bar chart on the right — total sales split by segment across periods.
A headline metric (title + a supporting statement) beside a line chart with labelled point markers and a trend line.
A statement beside two small stacked bar charts side by side — comparing two related measures (e.g. cash from operations vs. adjusted free cash flow) over two periods.
A wide holdings / positions table — symbol, name and a row of numeric columns — closed by a bold portfolio summary row.
A titled slide with two bar-chart panels side by side (small multiples) — the same measure across two cuts.
Two bar charts side by side (small multiples) — e.g. a commercial vs total view — each panelled with its own title.
A minimal section break: one large bold word (e.g. Appendix) marking a new part of the report.
A dense appendix table: named metric rows across many period columns (e.g. RPO, stock-based compensation by quarter).
A propositions / options wall: a caption+title head over up to five parallel text cards, one of which can be highlighted as the chosen option.
A strategy map / positioning canvas: four labelled quadrants of guiding questions meeting at a central proposition pill.
A long-range outlook: a row of horizon markers (Today → future years) drawn as boxes that grow with distance, introduced by a title + body paragraph.
Phased objectives: three (or more) cards — one per year / horizon — each with a short chevron-bulleted list of goals.
A phased plan laid out on a timeline: several phases across a dotted axis, with a row of dimensions (content, messaging …) filled in per phase.
A brand / strategy framework table: labelled rows that each span one wide cell or split into several columns (pillars), closing on a dense strip of topic markers.
A resource / cost allocation over time: a narrative + legend on the left, a multi-line trend chart with phase dividers on the right.
A Golden-Circle / why-how-what model: three nested rings on the left, each expanded into a labelled paragraph block on the right.
A brand-attribute / positioning scale: a stack of bipolar sliders (e.g. youthful ↔ mature) each marked with where the brand sits, explained by a left text column.
A layered onion model: nested circles sharing a base, each layer labelled with a title + line, explained by a right text column.
A stakeholder-proximity model: concentric rings radiating out from the centre (you) through team, community and beyond, explained by a left text column.
A three-lens Venn: three factors (e.g. opportunity, experience, expectations) overlapping on a central proposition, explained by a right text column.
A cyclical methodology: named stages placed on a dashed ring to show a repeating process, explained by a left text column.
A hierarchy / strategy pyramid: a stack of tiers from foundation to apex, explained by a title + body paragraph on the right.
A growth projection: a curve rising from a starting point to a set of future outcomes, anchored to a labelled month timeline.
A roadmap of escalating targets: filled milestone cards stepping up-and-right across a date timeline, with light placeholders for the space still ahead.
A roadmap opener: a horizontal week/milestone timeline with a highlighted 'today' marker and a short note beneath it.
A phased roadmap on a single axis: kickoff and successive phases, each with a month and a short note.
A roadmap of escalating milestones stepping up-and-right across a date timeline, with light placeholders for the ground still ahead.
A phased plan shown as a row of cards, with the current phase highlighted.
A phased journey drawn as a run of arches, each phase numbered with a short description below.
A one-line schedule: consecutive phase pills sized by duration across a few months, with a Today marker.
A sprint plan: sprints grouped by week, each week carrying a phase, with iteration markers, explained by a left text column.
A milestone timeline with photos: key moments placed above and below a central axis, each with an image, title and note.
A milestone timeline that spotlights one moment: the highlighted card stays full-strength while the others are muted.
A dense milestone timeline: ten photo moments stacked above and below the axis for a packed retrospective or roadmap.
A dense milestone timeline that spotlights one moment among ten, the rest muted.
A short-range Gantt: a handful of workstreams shown as bars across a few months.
An annual Gantt: workstreams shown as bars across all twelve months, grouped by quarter.
A weekly output / deliverables table: columns per week, each cell a short bulleted list, under a dark banner.
A content / channel plan matrix: KPI rows against channel columns, each cell a short bulleted list.
A year-at-a-glance calendar: four quarter columns, each holding three month cards with a headline.
An organisation chart: departments flanking a central core team of named people and working groups.
A leadership roster: a few featured leaders with larger portraits beside a grid of the wider team.
A row of four profile cards — a portrait over a name, title and short note.
A row of five profile cards — a portrait over a name, title and short note.
A propositions / options wall: a caption+title head over up to five parallel bulleted cards, one highlighted as chosen.
